extractedRows.sourceTitle: Disorders of Telomere Length.
extractedRows.exactClaimUse: Can support source-context framing that both short and ultra-long telomere length states can drive disease risk: short telomere length is associated with degenerative phenotypes such as immunodeficiency, bone marrow failure and pulmonary disease, while ultra-long telomere length can predispose to benign and malignant neoplasia.
extractedRows.endpointDefinition: Candidate endpoints include telomere length distribution, short telomere syndrome status, bone marrow failure, pulmonary disease, immunodeficiency, ultra-long-telomere variants and neoplasia incidence.
extractedRows.populationOrSetting: Children and adults with inherited or clinically suspected telomere length disorders; clinical review context rather than population-wide anti-aging intervention context.
extractedRows.effectOrMechanismSignal: Mechanism signal is boundary-setting: telomere shortening can constrain tissue renewal and drive degenerative disease, while excessive telomere length can extend replicative potential in ways that couple to neoplasia risk.
extractedRows.uncertaintyOrBias: The source is a 2026 clinical review with no open fulltext in automated access; it should not be used to estimate individual telomere length risk, anti-aging benefit or telomerase intervention safety without fulltext review.
extractedRows.transferBoundary: Transfer only to qualitative telomere-length boundary framing and cancer-degeneration coupling; do not transfer to personal telomere testing interpretation, telomerase activation claims or lifespan prediction.
